newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Nov 13.

text.p: NTT Mobile Communications Network Inc (NTT Do Co Mo) and its group companies plan to abolish sign-up fees for cellular phone services. They will apply to the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry for permission soon and hope to carry out the plan as early as December.

Nippon Thompson Co Ltd is expected to have increased its parent current profit by 3.8 times to around 2.7 billion yen in the first half year to September 30 from the year-ago period, helped by the yen's weakness.
NEC Corp and Texas Instruments Inc has agreed to jointly develop a large-scale integrated circuit system (LSI). The two companies plan to complete the project in two to three years.

Forty leading Japanese electronic product makers, including Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, Fujitsu Ltd and Mitsubishi Electric Corp, have decided to expand operational tests of a system to exchange information and data about electronic components through the Internet in Singapore, Malaysia, China and other Asian countries.
Matsushita Electric Works Ltd plans to shift all copper-laminated plate production to China and Thailand by spring 1997.
Canon Inc plans to enter the systems integration (SI) business, selling systems which link different makes of equipment.

Catena Corp plans to enter the call-back business for corporate customers after joining with Avirnex Communications Group of the United States in mid-November. It hopes to offer cheaper prices than those to be offered by AT&T Corp, which is also planning to enter the business.

Toray Industries Inc plans to increase imports of nylon continuous fiber to 150 tonnes a month from 100 tonnes in the second half year to March 31 to offset a domestic supply shortage. It will import the products from its Indonesian and Thai units.
